why: the loop fits b041's new pads before judging it (tuning trial 1 of 4)

This is a low-confidence probe of the last untested band. Angles 36 and 37.5 at reach 8 lost banana and gained nothing, so the threshold for the wide boxes likely sits near 38 and banana's near 34–35. At 33.5 the face at 85 mm comes to about +25 deg instead of +27, and banana's 38 mm face to about −8 deg instead of −6. If tuna, the shortest wide object at 34 mm with its top at +17, has any margin, this is where it would show without losing banana. If it gains nothing, that confirms no flat pad angle closes the gap and backs the rocker idea.

Angle 34.2 is the smallest step up from the kept 33.5. The rva000 pudding placement already passes at 33.5, and the reg placement misses by about 2 mm of contact height. +0.7 deg drops the tip about 0.4 mm and the face about 0.7 deg, which is the lowest-risk nudge toward flipping reg_pudding. Banana was lost only at 36 deg and up at reach 8, so 34.2 should stay on banana's safe side. No catalogue swap can do this: parallelogram tips rise +64 mm, long_slide skips teeth and overloads its bushings, prismatic reaches 53 mm, and 12 V servos are refused on budget.

This is the stronger version of the same lever: TPU 1.5 mm at angle 32.7 deg. Thinning by 1.5 mm per face adds 3 mm of opening, so maximum opening is about 99 mm. That lowers the tip about 3 mm at the wide end, and the lower angle gives back about 0.4 mm, for a net of about 2.6 mm. It tilts the mid-range face about 1.8 deg, or about 2 deg of pad angle, so banana sees about the tilt of 34.7 at 3 mm, inside the band that held. The wide-end face improves by only about 1 deg, so a sugar_box gain depends on tip height and opening mattering more than face tilt. Earlier gains at angles of 38 and up came with about 4 deg or more of face change, so sugar is a stretch. Mustard at 96 mm is unlikely, and I do not predict it.
